default_thresholds_note: Module 0 default thresholds. Applied by the application layer from admin config, NOT baked as UDF defaults (the UDF takes all five thresholds explicitly so a growth lead can tune aggressiveness without a SQL deploy). `heloc_equity_min_pct > min_equity_pct` is intentional — HELOC underwriting demands more equity cushion than plain refi. `retention_min_spread < min_spread_bps` is intentional — we reach out earlier on existing relationships.
product_labels_note: Contract for backend rendering. The UDF returns the lowercase code; the human label shown on Lead Queue, Borrower 360, and Offer Orchestrator surfaces comes from this map. The next slice (backend-databricks-engineer) should import this JSON and expose the label via OfferRecommendation.product_label.
label_shift_note: Previously mock_data.py hardcoded B-48294 (Park) as 'HELOC'. Under this decision tree, Park lands in 'refi_plus_heloc' (Refinance + HELOC) because a 188 bps spread AND 39% equity both clear their respective bars — a pure HELOC would leave refi revenue on the table. This is the honest output of the tree; the backend engineer will update mock_data.py to match. B-48291 (Rodriguez, 'Refinance + HELOC') and B-48295 (Thompson, 'Purchase Mortgage') are preserved.

cases.note: Listing dominates every other signal. Every other branch WOULD fire under these inputs (strong spread, strong equity, permit, investor, customer, competitor lien) — yet branch 1 wins because the active listing means the current lien is about to be paid off anyway. Pins the priority order.
Clean refi+HELOC cross-sell. Spread 120>=75 AND equity 45>=35 — no permit needed. Branch 2 fires above branch 3 because the refi economics drive the conversation regardless of permit.
Pure HELOC lane. Spread 30<75 so branch 2 fails; permit=TRUE AND equity 45>=35 so branch 3 fires. This is the 'permit, no refi need' story — renovation financing on an existing low-rate lien.

Plain refi. Economics 100>=75, but equity 20 is below heloc_equity_min=35, so branch 2 fails. No permit so branch 3 fails. Branch 4 fires: 100>=75 AND 20>=15. Lead with refi; leave HELOC cross-sell for later cycles.
Cash-out refi lane. No refi rate economics (20<75), no permit, equity 30 is below HELOC threshold (35) but above cashout threshold (25). Branch 5 fires.

Investor branch. Equity 10 is below every equity bar (refi min 15, cashout 25, HELOC 35) and no rate spread, so branches 2-5 all fail. Branch 6 fires on is_investor=TRUE. Pins that investor sits BELOW the owner-occupant equity branches.

Retention via competitor-lien recapture. No rate spread and low equity, but customer=TRUE AND competitor_lien=TRUE triggers branch 7 directly — a competitor lien on the Owner Link is a recapture signal even without rate economics.

Customer without strong rate OR competitor lien falls to nurture. Branch 7 requires customer=TRUE AND (spread 30>=50 OR competitor_lien) — 30<50 AND competitor=FALSE, so branch 7 fails. Keep in funnel, do not surface to approval queue.

Boundary: equity one below heloc_equity_min_pct (34 vs 35). Branch 2 fails on 34<35, branch 3 fails (no permit), branch 4 fires: 100>=75 AND 34>=15. Paired with case_10; flipping equity 34->35 shifts refi -> refi_plus_heloc.

Boundary: equity EXACTLY at heloc_equity_min_pct (35). The >= contract means exact equality is IN. Flipping to strict > would fail this case loudly. Paired with case_09 to pin the HELOC equity boundary on both sides.

Fixture borrower B-48291 (Rodriguez). Spread 88 and equity 46 come from fn_rate_spread and the LTV calc pinned in rate_spread/in_the_money fixtures. Branch 2 fires (88>=75 AND 46>=35) -> 'refi_plus_heloc' -> 'Refinance + HELOC'. PRESERVES the fixture label.

Fixture borrower B-48294 (Park). LABEL SHIFT from previously hardcoded 'HELOC'. Under the tree: spread 188>=75 AND equity 39>=35 so branch 2 fires BEFORE the pure-HELOC branch 3, returning 'refi_plus_heloc' -> 'Refinance + HELOC'. This is the honest output of the decision tree — when rate economics also qualify, the cross-sell is the correct product, not pure HELOC. Backend engineer will update mock_data.py to match.

Fixture borrower B-48295 (Thompson). listed_for_sale=TRUE so branch 1 fires immediately -> 'purchase' -> 'Purchase Mortgage'. PRESERVES the fixture label. Even though spread 162 and equity 56 would otherwise qualify for refi_plus_heloc, the listing dominates.

All-NULL row. Numerics coerce to 0, booleans coerce to FALSE. Branch 1 FALSE; branch 2: 0>=75 FALSE; branch 3: FALSE; branch 4: 0>=75 FALSE; branch 5: 0>=25 FALSE; branch 6: FALSE; branch 7: FALSE. Falls through to 'nurture' — the safe lane. Pins NULL policy and keeps recommended_offer NOT NULL downstream.

Same inputs as case_02 but min_spread_bps raised from 75 to 150. Branch 2 fails (120<150), branch 3 fails (no permit), branch 4 fails (120<150), branch 5 fires (45>=25) -> 'cash_out'. Proves thresholds come from the caller, not baked constants — a stricter admin config demotes a refi_plus_heloc lead to cash_out.
Threshold NULLs fail closed before the decision tree. Missing rules must not coerce to 0 and make 0>=0 qualify a borrower for refi_plus_heloc; the safe lane is nurture.
